name: Kit Gill
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember a shower key returned wrapped in a little towel.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Kit by a small Tuesday habit. Kit can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I loaned him the key to the workshop shower. He returned it because he wanted to pay for an ordinary membership.
appearance: Kit is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Kit listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Kit uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Kit well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To get the boat owner a normal shower membership.
family: Louise Hooper is Kit’s younger cousin. Kit asks before bringing somebody along. Louise can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Louise says, “I am the junior worker who polished the scarred hand.”
connections: Fiona Salas. The spare shower key means something different to somebody who once spent a winter as a supposed visitor.
